training-data.hint: The important distinction is the data's role, format, or fitness for the real population; those details determine what can be learned and whether evaluation is trustworthy.

training-data-01.label: The portion of data used to learn model parameters.
training-data-01.why: The portion of data used to learn model parameters.

training-data-02.label: Held-out data used during development to compare choices and tune hyperparameters.
training-data-02.why: Held-out data used during development to compare choices and tune hyperparameters.

training-data-03.label: Untouched data used at the end to estimate performance on unseen examples.
training-data-03.why: Untouched data used at the end to estimate performance on unseen examples.

training-data-04.label: Examples that include the target answer required for supervised learning.
training-data-04.why: Examples that include the target answer required for supervised learning.

training-data-05.label: Examples without target answers, often used for unsupervised or self-supervised learning.
training-data-05.why: Examples without target answers, often used for unsupervised or self-supervised learning.

training-data-06.label: Data organized into defined fields, rows, columns, or records.
training-data-06.why: Data organized into defined fields, rows, columns, or records.

training-data-07.label: Free-form content such as text, images, audio, and video.
training-data-07.why: Free-form content such as text, images, audio, and video.

training-data-08.label: Examples that reflect the people, conditions, and cases the model will encounter in use.
training-data-08.why: Examples that reflect the people, conditions, and cases the model will encounter in use.

training-data-09.label: Information unavailable at prediction time accidentally enters training and inflates measured performance.
training-data-09.why: Information unavailable at prediction time accidentally enters training and inflates measured performance.

training-data-10.label: One target class appears much more often than another, making accuracy potentially misleading.
training-data-10.why: One target class appears much more often than another, making accuracy potentially misleading.
